solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Force of evil once let loose

indicators.note: Letters let loose are freed from their order and can fall anywhere.

parts.note: Taken as written.
Taken as written.

explanation.surface: A sinister power, once held in check, has been unleashed on the world.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes both words, EVIL and ONCE, eight letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: brute force used to harm is exactly what this word names.

clue.text: Female elephant scoffing hot dog

indicators.note: To scoff is to eat greedily, and what is eaten ends up inside the eater.

parts.note: A female elephant, like a female whale or cow, is called a cow.
H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps.

explanation.surface: A cow elephant wolfing down a hot dog at the fair.
explanation.walkthrough: "Hot dog" looks like a snack, but it splits: hot is the eaten letter and dog is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this is a Chinese breed of dog with a blue-black tongue.

clue.text: What prisoner might long for, eh?

definitions.meaning: An official release from a sentence, the thing every convict hopes for.
A request to repeat what was said, in its politer form.

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a single interjection, so the answer must work as an exclamation too.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an official forgiveness that frees a convict, and the polite word for asking someone to say it again.

clue.text: Fed up with border guard

parts.note: FED written upwards, as this is a down clue.
An end is a boundary or edge.

explanation.surface: Someone sick of the job of watching the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: "Fed up" reads as bored, but in a down clue "up" turns FED upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to protect from attack.

clue.text: Crackpot oriental aunt?

indicators.note: A crackpot is crazy, so the letters that follow are in a crazy order.

parts.note: Taken as written.

explanation.surface: An eccentric aunt from the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that an aunt is only one example, a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an aunt is one member of the family, and the answer covers any such kin.

clue.text: Gossip with Jean-Paul Sartre's feline friend?

definitions.meaning: Sartre was French, so this is the French word for cat.

explanation.surface: Swapping gossip with the philosopher Sartre's pet cat.
explanation.walkthrough: Sartre is there only to signal French; the question mark flags that the second meaning is in another language.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an English word for light talk, and a foreign word, the French for cat.

clue.text: Sikh cafe cooking your supper?

indicators.note: Cooking turns ingredients into something new, so the letters get rearranged.

parts.note: Taken as written.
Taken as written.

explanation.surface: A Sikh-run café preparing your evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose, hence the question mark: supper could be many things.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example, reversed: supper is a meal, and a patty of fish and potato is one thing it might be.

clue.text: Reminder of the code word for an E

definitions.meaning: Something that recalls an earlier thing, as in a faint repeat of the past.

definitions.text: the code word for an E
definitions.meaning: The NATO phonetic alphabet word for the fifth letter.

explanation.surface: A memo noting the radio code word for the letter E.
explanation.walkthrough: The NATO alphabet (Alpha, Bravo, Charlie...) spells letters over radio, one word per letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a trace that recalls something earlier, and the radio alphabet's word for E.

clue.text: The Speaker's flummoxed, displaying weakness

indicators.note: What a speaker says is heard rather than read.

parts.note: Floored means baffled; in a British accent, which drops the R, it is said the same as the answer.

explanation.surface: The Commons Speaker, baffled, shows a moment of weakness.
explanation.walkthrough: "The Speaker" suggests the House of Commons chair, but here it is anyone speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something with a defect shows a weakness.

clue.text: Former wife finishing with Bill? Spot on

parts.note: An ex is a former partner.
A bill becomes an act once it is passed by Parliament.

explanation.surface: An ex-wife ending up with a man called Bill, a perfect match.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man's name, but it is a parliamentary bill, and "finishing with" means it comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: spot on is the informal way of saying precisely right.

clue.text: Sad when daughter goes? That's personal

indicators.note: When the daughter goes she leaves, so her letter is taken away.

parts.note: Down means low in spirits.
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter.

explanation.surface: Feeling low once the daughter leaves home is a private matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The departing daughter is the first letter of DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as adjectives: my personal car is my own car.

clue.text: Trainee in the wrong from time to time

indicators.note: Something done from time to time happens at intervals, so only every other letter is used.

parts.note: The odd letters of the three words, starting with the first.

explanation.surface: A trainee who has got something wrong at work.
explanation.walkthrough: "In" looks like a link word but its letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, mainly American: a junior doctor or student gaining work experience is a trainee.

clue.text: Outrage of Tory men I abused

indicators.note: Letters that are abused are mistreated and knocked out of shape.

parts.note: Taken as written.
Taken as written.
Taken as written.

explanation.surface: Public fury after a man complains that Conservative men mistreated him.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer strictly means great wickedness, not just great size, which is why it fits here.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the strict sense: a monstrous wrong or atrocious act.

clue.text: Club for AA member?

definitions.meaning: The golf club used for long shots from the tee.
The AA (Automobile Association) is a British breakdown service whose members are motorists.

explanation.surface: A club open to members of Alcoholics Anonymous.
explanation.walkthrough: AA suggests Alcoholics Anonymous; here it is the Automobile Association, the UK breakdown service.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a golf club, and a motorist who might belong to a motoring organisation.

clue.text: Leak from European delegation

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for European.
A group sent on official business.

explanation.surface: A secret leaked by an EU delegation.
explanation.walkthrough: Leak reads as a news leak, but here it is a noun for something escaping, like gas.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: gas or fluid escaping from a pipe is given off, a discharge.

clue.text: Woman in Madrid's preposterous reason

indicators.note: Something preposterous is absurd, so the letters are in an absurd order.

parts.note: Taken as written.

explanation.surface: A Spanish woman giving an absurd excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: Madrid signals Spanish, so the answer is a Spanish word.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreign word: the Spanish title for a married woman, the equivalent of Mrs.

clue.text: A body of water overseas

parts.note: Taken as written.
The Norfolk lakes in eastern England, formed where rivers widen, are each called by this name.

explanation.surface: A lake or sea far away in a foreign land.
explanation.walkthrough: The Norfolk Broads are a well-known English lake district, so BROAD is a fair body of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: being in a foreign country, across the sea.

clue.text: Reportedly excluded Italian, a crook

indicators.note: What is reported is heard second-hand, so the word counts by its sound.

parts.note: Banned means excluded, and a musical group is said the same way.
IT is the standard abbreviation for Italian.

explanation.surface: An Italian excluded, it is said, for being a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: Only "excluded" is heard; Italian adds its letters as they are spelt.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an armed robber, a criminal.

clue.text: Harry, a character in Wind in the Willows

definitions.meaning: Used as a verb: to pester persistently.

definitions.text: a character in Wind in the Willows
definitions.meaning: Kenneth Grahame's novel has animal heroes: Mole, Rat, Toad and a gruff older friend.

explanation.surface: A figure named Harry in the classic children's tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry poses as a name but is the verb meaning to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a verb for nagging someone, and the wise old animal in Grahame's riverbank story.

clue.text: Airline covering up a beastly cry

indicators.note: What covers something up goes round it and hides it inside.

parts.note: BA is British Airways.
Taken as written.

explanation.surface: An airline hushing up a terrible scream from a passenger.
explanation.walkthrough: "Beastly" looks like disapproval but literally means belonging to a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a sheep's bleat is one cry made by a beast.

clue.text: Poet has house by river

parts.note: A home is a house.
R is the standard abbreviation for river.

explanation.surface: A poet owns a house beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: "By" places the river's letter next to the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the ancient Greek author of the Iliad and the Odyssey.

clue.text: Beautiful woman ignoring one for a time

indicators.note: Ignoring the one means leaving it out.

parts.note: A houri is a beautiful young woman, from the maidens of the Islamic paradise.
I is the Roman numeral one.

explanation.surface: A beauty snubbing someone for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: HOURI is a crossword favourite for a beautiful woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: sixty minutes is one particular span of time.

clue.text: Good-looking chap holding article from Copenhagen?

indicators.note: What holds something has it inside.

parts.note: A dish is slang for an attractive person.
An is the indefinite article.

explanation.surface: A handsome man carrying something he bought in Copenhagen.
explanation.walkthrough: "Article" suggests a thing he carries, but it is the grammar word; the question mark admits Copenhagen is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Copenhagen is Denmark's capital, so anything from there belongs to Denmark.

clue.text: Inquisitive boss regularly visiting New York

indicators.note: A visitor goes into a place, so these letters go inside.

parts.note: NY is the standard abbreviation for New York.

indicators.note: Regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept.

parts.note: The second and fourth letters.

explanation.surface: A prying boss on a trip to New York.
explanation.walkthrough: "Boss" wants to be the person who is nosy, but it is only raw letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: prying into other people's business.

clue.text: The smallest one's somewhat disgruntled

indicators.note: Somewhat means to some extent, so only part of the next word is used.

parts.note: The letters sit in the middle of the word, after DISG.

explanation.surface: The littlest one is a bit grumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes "somewhat" qualify the grumpiness, but it points into the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the weakest, smallest animal of a litter.

clue.text: Dislike analyst's initial interpretation

indicators.note: An initial is a first letter.

parts.note: The first letter of analyst.
One person's account or reading of events.

explanation.surface: A dislike of how an analyst first interpreted something.
explanation.walkthrough: "Initial" reads as early, but it means just the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a strong feeling of distaste.
